title: Resisting the Devil
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Resisting the devil means submitting to God and standing against Satan’s lies, temptations, accusations, and schemes by faith, Scripture, prayer, and steadfast obedience.
summary: Resisting the devil means submitting to God and standing against Satan’s lies, temptations, accusations, and schemes by faith, Scripture, prayer, and steadfast obedience.
christFocus: Jesus Christ resisted Satan perfectly and defeated him decisively. Believers resist not by personal power, but by standing in Christ and trusting His Word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture commands believers to resist the devil. This resistance begins with submission to God. A person cannot faithfully oppose Satan while clinging to rebellion against the Lord.

Resisting the devil requires sober watchfulness. Satan is described as an adversary who prowls, schemes, tempts, and seeks opportunity. Believers must not be careless with sin, anger, bitterness, or deception.

Jesus resisted Satan with Scripture and obedience to the Father. His example shows that resistance is not loud performance, but faithful trust in God’s Word under pressure.

Believers resist from a place of victory in Christ. The devil is real, but he is not sovereign. God gives grace to the humble and strength to stand.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people try to resist spiritual attack while still making peace with sin. Scripture calls for both resistance and submission to God.

This doctrine gives practical help. Believers do not need to fear the devil as though he rules them. They need to stand firm, reject lies, and stay near Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Submit yourself to God and resist the devil quickly. Do not give him room through hidden sin, bitterness, pride, or isolation. Answer lies with Scripture, confess sin, pray for help, and stand with other believers in faith.
